==============================================================================
$ catnip --help
==============================================================================
Usage: catnip [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...

  CatSniffer: All in one catnip tools environment.

Options:
  -v, --verbose  Increase logging verbosity. Repeatable: -v (INFO), -vv (DEBUG +
                 timestamps).
  -h, --help     Show this message and exit.

Commands:
  cativity    IQ Activity Monitor
  completion  Install shell tab completion for catnip.
  devices     List connected CatSniffer devices
  flash       Flash CC1352 Firmware or list available firmware images.
  identify    Send identification command to CatSniffer device
  lora        LoRa SX1262 tools
  meshtastic  Meshtastic protocol tools
  restore     Restore CC1352 when bootloader is broken.
  setup-env   Setup environment: install udev rules and add user to groups.
  sniff       Sniffer protocol control
  spam        BLE advertising-spam control (CC1352P7 'ble_spam' firmware).
  status      Show board, firmware and capabilities detected on a CatSniffer.
  update      Check and update RP2040 firmware to match the latest release.
  verify      Verify CatSniffer device functionality
  vhci        VHCI Bridge - Expose CatSniffer as hciX.

  Set CATNIP_DEBUG=1 to see a full traceback instead of a one-line error.

  Examples:
    catnip devices                  # list connected CatSniffers
    catnip status                   # firmware + capabilities on a device
    catnip flash --list             # see available firmware images
    catnip sniff ble                # sniff BLE traffic
    catnip spam start --mode apple  # BLE advertising spam (authorised use)
    catnip -v sniff zigbee -c 15    # same, with INFO-level logging

$ catnip flash --help
==============================================================================
Usage: catnip flash [OPTIONS] [FIRMWARE]

  Flash CC1352 Firmware or list available firmware images.

  Examples:
      catnip flash --list               # images this board can take
      catnip flash --list --all         # the whole catalogue
      catnip flash ble                  # flash Sniffle BLE firmware
      catnip flash zigbee --device 1    # flash TI sniffer to device #1
      catnip flash ble --board v2       # name the board when its shell is dead
      catnip flash --refresh            # update the cache to the latest release
      catnip flash --refresh --force    # wipe the cache and redownload it

Options:
  -d, --device INTEGER  Device ID (for multiple CatSniffers). If not specified,
                        first device will be selected.
  -l, --list            List available firmware images to flash
  --full                Show full descriptions without truncation in the list
  --all                 With --list, show the whole catalogue instead of only
                        the images that can be flashed on the connected board
  --refresh             Check GitHub for a newer firmware release now and
                        download it if there is one.
  --force               With --refresh: wipe the local firmware cache and re-
                        download everything from scratch.
  --board [v2|v3]       Board generation override (v2 = SAMD21 + CC1352P1, v3 =
                        RP2040 + CC1352P7). Only needed when the Cat-Shell port
                        cannot answer; the wrong value disables the CC1352
                        bootloader
  -h, --help            Show this message and exit.

  LoRa SX1262 tools

Options:

Commands:
  scan      Sweep SF/BW/frequency combinations and count packets on each.
  spectrum  Live Spectrum Scanner for SX1262 - Real-time frequency spectrum...

==============================================================================
$ catnip lora scan --help
==============================================================================
Usage: catnip lora scan [OPTIONS]

  Sweep SF/BW/frequency combinations and count packets on each.

  A LoRa receiver only demodulates a frame whose spreading factor, bandwidth,
  frequency and sync word it already matches, so finding the settings of an
  unknown transmitter means trying them.  This does the trying: the host retunes
  the SX1262 between combinations while the firmware keeps streaming, and the
  live table shows which combination is hearing anything.

  Examples:
      catnip lora scan                          # 915 MHz, every SF and BW
      catnip lora scan --dwell 8                # slow traffic, longer look
      catnip lora scan -f 868.1,868.3,868.5     # the EU channels
      catnip lora scan --sf 7,9 --bw 125        # narrow the search
      catnip lora scan -sw 0x2B -f 906.875      # look for Meshtastic
      catnip lora scan --passes 0               # keep sweeping until Ctrl+C

Options:
  -d, --device INTEGER    Device ID (for multiple CatSniffers)
  -f, --freq TEXT         Frequencies to sweep, comma separated, in MHz
                          (868.1,915) or Hz (915000000). Default: 915
  --sf TEXT               Spreading factors to sweep, comma separated (7-12).
                          Default: all
  --bw TEXT               Bandwidths to sweep in kHz, comma separated
                          (125,250,500). Default: all
  --dwell FLOAT RANGE     Seconds to listen on each combination (default: 3). A
                          single SF12/BW125 frame is over a second on air — give
                          the slow end more  [0.2<=x<=120]
  --passes INTEGER RANGE  Number of full sweeps; 0 repeats until Ctrl+C
                          (default: 1)  [0<=x<=1000]
  -sw, --sync-word TEXT   LoRa sync word: 'private' (0x12), 'public' (0x34,
                          LoRaWAN) or any raw byte as 0xNN (e.g. 0x2B for
                          Meshtastic). Default: private.
  -h, --help              Show this message and exit.

$ catnip restore --help
==============================================================================
Usage: catnip restore [OPTIONS] [FIRMWARE]

  Restore CC1352 when bootloader is broken.

  Uses RP2040 as CMSIS-DAP JTAG programmer via OpenOCD to flash the CC1352
  directly. Requires OpenOCD installed. Only v3 boards can do this: a v2
  (SAMD21) has no RP2040 to load the probe onto and needs an external cJTAG
  programmer instead.

  If no firmware is specified, uses the default CatSniffer firmware from the
  catnip release.

  Example:
      catnip restore                    # default CatSniffer firmware
      catnip restore firmware.hex       # custom firmware
      catnip restore firmware.hex -d 1  # specific device
      catnip restore --board v3         # name the board when its shell is dead

Options:
  -d, --device INTEGER  Device ID (for shell access to trigger BOOTSEL)
  --tapid TEXT          CC1352 JTAG TAPID (default: CC1352P7)
  --board [v2|v3]       Board generation override (v2 = SAMD21 + CC1352P1, v3 =
                        RP2040 + CC1352P7). Only needed when the Cat-Shell port
                        cannot answer; the wrong value disables the CC1352
                        bootloader
  -h, --help            Show this message and exit.

  Requires root privileges (sudo). This command installs the necessary udev

  'dialout' and 'bluetooth' groups.

Options:
  -h, --help  Show this message and exit.

$ catnip sniff fsk --help
==============================================================================
Usage: catnip sniff fsk [OPTIONS]

  Sniffing (G)FSK with Sniffer SX1262 firmware.

  Same radio and same ports as ``sniff lora``, with the SX1262 in FSK mode —
  where it hears the sub-GHz traffic LoRa cannot: 802.15.4g/Wi-SUN, smart
  meters, alarm and sensor links, and anything else on a plain (G)FSK ISM
  channel.  Unlike LoRa, FSK only demodulates what matches the bitrate,
  deviation and sync word it was told to expect, so those have to be right.

  Examples:
      catnip sniff fsk                             # defaults: 915MHz, 50kbps
      catnip sniff fsk -freq 868000000 -br 100000 -fd 50000
      catnip sniff fsk -sw 2DD4 --whitening        # 802.15.4g-style framing
      catnip sniff fsk -ws                         # live Wireshark
      catnip sniff fsk -l                          # live panel instead of hex
      catnip sniff fsk -w capture.pcapng           # save it, offer to open it
      catnip sniff fsk --bt off                    # plain FSK, no shaping
      catnip sniff fsk --profile home-meter-fsk    # user profile
      catnip sniff fsk -freq 868000000 --save-profile mi-fsk

Options:
  -ws, --wireshark                Open Wireshark live while the capture runs
                                  (LoRaTap over a local pipe)
  -oc, --open-capture             Open the capture in Wireshark when the sniffer
                                  stops. Without --write the packets are saved
                                  to a temporary .pcapng file first
  -v, --verbose                   Show verbose output in terminal
  -l, --live                      Show a live panel while capturing — packets/s,
                                  last and best link quality, an RSSI histogram
                                  and the last frames — instead of the scrolling
                                  packet dump
  -P, --profile TEXT              Fill in radio defaults from a named profile —
                                  built-in region/protocol presets (see 'catnip
                                  sniff profiles'), or your own in
                                  ~/.config/catnip/profiles.toml. Flags you pass
                                  explicitly still override it.
  --save-profile NAME             Save this command's radio settings (after
                                  --profile and any explicit flags are merged)
                                  as NAME in ~/.config/catnip/profiles.toml, for
                                  later use as --profile NAME.
  -freq, --frequency INTEGER RANGE
                                  Frequency in Hz, 137-1020 MHz (e.g., 915000000
                                  for 915 MHz)  [137000000<=x<=1020000000]
  -br, --bitrate INTEGER RANGE    Bitrate in bps (600-300000). Default: 50000.
                                  [600<=x<=300000]
  -fd, --fdev INTEGER RANGE       Frequency deviation in Hz (600-200000).
                                  Default: 25000.  [600<=x<=200000]
  -bw, --bandwidth [4.8|5.8|7.3|9.7|11.7|14.6|19.5|23.4|29.3|39.0|46.9|58.6|78.2|93.8|117.3|156.2|187.2|234.3|312.0|373.6|467.0]
                                  RX bandwidth in kHz. Must cover bitrate + 2x
                                  deviation or the firmware widens it to 187.2.
                                  Default: 187.2.
  -pw, --tx_power INTEGER RANGE   TX Power in dBm (-9 to 22, SX1262 hardware
                                  range)  [-9<=x<=22]
  -pre, --preamble INTEGER RANGE  Preamble length in bytes (FSK counts bytes,
                                  not symbols). Default: 8.  [0<=x<=65535]
  -sw, --sync-word TEXT           FSK sync word: 1-8 bytes of hex (e.g. 2DD4 for
                                  802.15.4g/Meshtastic). Default: 12AD.
  --bt [off|0.3|0.5|0.7|1.0]      Gaussian filter BT: 'off' is plain FSK, a
                                  value is GFSK. Default: 0.5.
  --crc / --no-crc                Let the modem verify the CRC and drop failing
                                  frames. Default: --no-crc.
  --whitening / --no-whitening    Undo the transmitter's data whitening.
                                  Default: --no-whitening.
  --pktlen [variable|fixed]       'variable' reads each frame's length from its
                                  header, 'fixed' assumes --payload bytes.
                                  Default: variable.
  --payload INTEGER RANGE         Payload length for --pktlen fixed, maximum
                                  length otherwise. Default: 255.  [1<=x<=255]
  -d, --device INTEGER            Device ID (for multiple CatSniffers)
  -r, --raw FILE                  Save captured packets as raw hex to FILE (RX:
                                  <hex> | RSSI: <rssi>)
  -ascii, --ascii FILE            Save captured packets as decoded ASCII to FILE
                                  (RX: <ascii> | RSSI: <rssi>)
  -w, --write FILE                Write the capture to FILE for offline analysis
                                  (.pcap, or .pcapng if the name ends in
                                  .pcapng). Works with or without --wireshark
  -f, --force                     Overwrite the --write file if it already
                                  exists
  -h, --help                      Show this message and exit.

==============================================================================
$ catnip sniff lora --help
==============================================================================
Usage: catnip sniff lora [OPTIONS]

  Sniffing LoRa with Sniffer SX1262 firmware.

  Examples:
      catnip sniff lora                          # defaults: 915MHz, SF7, BW125
      catnip sniff lora -freq 868000000 -sf 9
      catnip sniff lora -ws                      # live Wireshark while sniffing
      catnip sniff lora -l                       # live panel instead of hex
      catnip sniff lora -oc                      # sniff, then open Wireshark
      catnip sniff lora -w capture.pcapng        # save it, offer to open it
      catnip sniff lora -sw public               # LoRaWAN sync word (0x34)
      catnip sniff lora -sw 0x2B -pre 16         # Meshtastic sync word
      catnip sniff lora -sw public --iq inverted # LoRaWAN downlinks
      catnip sniff lora --profile eu868-meshtastic-longfast
      catnip sniff lora -P us915-meshtastic-shortfast -pw 10  # override tx_power only
      catnip sniff lora -freq 868000000 -sf 9 --save-profile mi-perfil

Options:
  -ws, --wireshark                Open Wireshark live while the capture runs
                                  (LoRaTap over a local pipe)
  -oc, --open-capture             Open the capture in Wireshark when the sniffer
                                  stops. Without --write the packets are saved
                                  to a temporary .pcapng file first
  -v, --verbose                   Show verbose output in terminal
  -l, --live                      Show a live panel while capturing — packets/s,
                                  last and best link quality, an RSSI histogram
                                  and the last frames — instead of the scrolling
                                  packet dump
  -P, --profile TEXT              Fill in radio defaults from a named profile —
                                  built-in region/protocol presets (see 'catnip
                                  sniff profiles'), or your own in
                                  ~/.config/catnip/profiles.toml. Flags you pass
                                  explicitly still override it.
  --save-profile NAME             Save this command's radio settings (after
                                  --profile and any explicit flags are merged)
                                  as NAME in ~/.config/catnip/profiles.toml, for
                                  later use as --profile NAME.
  -freq, --frequency INTEGER RANGE
                                  Frequency in Hz, 150-960 MHz (e.g., 915000000
                                  for 915 MHz)  [150000000<=x<=960000000]
  -bw, --bandwidth [125|250|500]  Bandwidth in kHz
  -sf, --spread_factor INTEGER RANGE
                                  Spreading Factor (7-12)  [7<=x<=12]
  -cr, --coding_rate INTEGER RANGE
                                  Coding Rate (5-8)  [5<=x<=8]
  -pw, --tx_power INTEGER RANGE   TX Power in dBm (-9 to 22, SX1262 hardware
                                  range)  [-9<=x<=22]
  -d, --device INTEGER            Device ID (for multiple CatSniffers)
  -sw, --sync-word TEXT           LoRa sync word: 'public' (0x34, LoRaWAN),
                                  'private' (0x12) or any raw byte as 0xNN (e.g.
                                  0x2B for Meshtastic). Default: private.
  -pre, --preamble INTEGER RANGE  Preamble length in symbols (6-65535). Default:
                                  12.  [6<=x<=65535]
  --iq [normal|inverted]          IQ polarity. LoRaWAN downlinks need
                                  'inverted'. Default: normal.
  -r, --raw FILE                  Save captured packets as raw hex to FILE (RX:
                                  <hex> | RSSI: <rssi> | SNR: <snr>)
  -ascii, --ascii FILE            Save captured packets as decoded ASCII to FILE
                                  (RX: <ascii> | RSSI: <rssi> | SNR: <snr>)
  -w, --write FILE                Write the capture to FILE for offline analysis
                                  (.pcap, or .pcapng if the name ends in
                                  .pcapng). Works with or without --wireshark
  -f, --force                     Overwrite the --write file if it already
                                  exists
  -h, --help                      Show this message and exit.

==============================================================================
$ catnip sniff profiles --help
==============================================================================
Usage: catnip sniff profiles [OPTIONS]

  List radio profiles available to --profile (built-in and user-defined).

  User profiles come from ~/.config/catnip/profiles.toml (or
  $CATNIP_PROFILES_FILE), as [profiles.NAME] tables; a name also used by a
  built-in profile overrides it.

  Examples:
      catnip sniff profiles
      catnip sniff profiles -c fsk

Options:
  -c, --command [lora|fsk]  Only list profiles for this radio mode
  -h, --help                Show this message and exit.

==============================================================================
$ catnip spam --help
==============================================================================
Usage: catnip spam [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...

  BLE advertising-spam control (CC1352P7 'ble_spam' firmware).

  Examples:
      catnip spam modes                     # list vendor modes (no hardware)
      catnip spam start --mode apple        # select Apple mode and emit
      catnip spam run --mode apple          # emit with a live view (Ctrl+C)
      catnip spam status                    # mode / running / model count
      catnip spam stop                      # stop emitting

  Use only on devices you own or are authorised to test.

Options:
  -h, --help  Show this message and exit.

Commands:
  modes   List the available vendor modes (no device needed).
  run     Start emitting and show a live view of the cycle (Ctrl+C to stop).
  start   Select a mode and start emitting.
  status  Report the current mode, running state and model count.
  stop    Stop emitting.

==============================================================================
$ catnip spam modes --help
==============================================================================
Usage: catnip spam modes [OPTIONS]

  List the available vendor modes (no device needed).

Options:
  -h, --help  Show this message and exit.

==============================================================================
$ catnip spam run --help
==============================================================================
Usage: catnip spam run [OPTIONS]

  Start emitting and show a live view of the cycle (Ctrl+C to stop).

  Unlike ``start``, this is an interactive session: it always stops the firmware
  and closes the port on exit, so the hardware is never left emitting.

Options:
  -d, --device INTEGER            Device ID (for multiple CatSniffers)
  -m, --mode [all|apple|android|windows|samsung]
                                  Vendor advertising set to emit.  [default:
                                  all]
  -b, --baudrate INTEGER          Override the bridge baudrate (default:
                                  firmware value, 921600).
  -y, --yes                       Skip the authorised-use confirmation prompt.
  -h, --help                      Show this message and exit.

==============================================================================
$ catnip spam start --help
==============================================================================
Usage: catnip spam start [OPTIONS]

  Select a mode and start emitting.

  Leaves the firmware emitting after the command returns; run ``catnip spam
  stop`` to halt it.

Options:
  -d, --device INTEGER            Device ID (for multiple CatSniffers)
  -m, --mode [all|apple|android|windows|samsung]
                                  Vendor advertising set to emit.  [default:
                                  all]
  -b, --baudrate INTEGER          Override the bridge baudrate (default:
                                  firmware value, 921600).
  -y, --yes                       Skip the authorised-use confirmation prompt.
  -h, --help                      Show this message and exit.

==============================================================================
$ catnip spam status --help
==============================================================================
Usage: catnip spam status [OPTIONS]

  Report the current mode, running state and model count.

Options:
  -d, --device INTEGER    Device ID (for multiple CatSniffers)
  -b, --baudrate INTEGER  Override the bridge baudrate (default: firmware value,
                          921600).
  -h, --help              Show this message and exit.

$ catnip spam stop --help
==============================================================================
Usage: catnip spam stop [OPTIONS]

  Stop emitting.

Options:
  -d, --device INTEGER    Device ID (for multiple CatSniffers)
  -b, --baudrate INTEGER  Override the bridge baudrate (default: firmware value,
                          921600).
  -h, --help              Show this message and exit.

==============================================================================
$ catnip status --help
==============================================================================
Usage: catnip status [OPTIONS]

  Show board, firmware and capabilities detected on a CatSniffer.

  Honest by design (Bombercat's `status` pattern, see analisis-bombercat-vs-
  catnip.md, section 7): unlike `sniff`/`flash`, which check for *one specific*
  firmware and flash it if missing, this only reports what it can actually
  confirm on the device right now, and says "unknown" rather than guessing.

  Examples:
      catnip status                 # first connected device
      catnip status --device 1      # a specific device by ID
      catnip status --diagnostics   # add the v2 stack/thread dump

Options:
  -d, --device INTEGER  Device ID (for multiple CatSniffers)
  -D, --diagnostics     Also dump the per-thread stack report and the trace ring
                        (only v2 boards report them)
  -h, --help            Show this message and exit.

==============================================================================
$ catnip update --help
==============================================================================
Usage: catnip update [OPTIONS]

  Check and update RP2040 firmware to match the latest release.

  Verifies that the RP2040 firmware version is compatible with the tool and the
  latest firmware release. If outdated, automatically updates the device.

  If the device is not detected, provides instructions to manually enter Boot
  Mode for recovery.

  Examples:
      catnip update              # check and update if outdated
      catnip update --force      # reflash regardless of version
      catnip update --board v2   # name the board when its shell is dead

Options:
  -d, --device INTEGER  Device ID (for multiple CatSniffers)
  -f, --force           Force update even if firmware versions match
  --board [v2|v3]       Board generation override (v2 = SAMD21 + CC1352P1, v3 =
                        RP2040 + CC1352P7). Only needed when the Cat-Shell port
                        cannot answer; the wrong value disables the CC1352
                        bootloader
  -h, --help            Show this message and exit.

==============================================================================
$ catnip verify --help
==============================================================================
Usage: catnip verify [OPTIONS]

  Verify CatSniffer device functionality

  Tests all connected CatSniffers and verifies: - Basic shell commands (help,
  status, lora_config, lora_mode) - LoRa configuration (frequency, SF, BW, etc.)
  - LoRa communication (TEST, TXTEST, TX commands)

  Use --test-all for comprehensive testing.

  Examples:
      catnip verify                # quick check of all connected devices
      catnip verify --test-all     # full LoRa config + communication tests
      catnip verify --device 1     # test only device #1

Options:
  --test-all            Run all tests including LoRa configuration and
                        communication
  -d, --device INTEGER  Test only a specific device (by ID)
  -q, --quiet           Show only summary results
  -h, --help            Show this message and exit.

==============================================================================
$ catnip vhci --help
==============================================================================
Usage: catnip vhci [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...

  VHCI Bridge - Expose CatSniffer as hciX.

  Requires sudo and the hci_vhci kernel module.

      sudo modprobe hci_vhci
      sudo python3 catnip.py vhci start

Options:
  -h, --help  Show this message and exit.

Commands:
  check  Check VHCI bridge prerequisites (kernel module, /dev/vhci, root,...
  start  Start the VHCI bridge — CatSniffer appears as hciX.

==============================================================================
$ catnip vhci check --help
==============================================================================
Usage: catnip vhci check [OPTIONS]

  Check VHCI bridge prerequisites (kernel module, /dev/vhci, root, packages).

Options:
  -h, --help  Show this message and exit.

==============================================================================
$ catnip vhci start --help
==============================================================================
Usage: catnip vhci start [OPTIONS]

  Start the VHCI bridge — CatSniffer appears as hciX.

  Requires root privileges and the hci_vhci kernel module:

      sudo modprobe hci_vhci
      sudo catnip vhci start
      hciconfig -a

  Compatible tools: bluetoothctl, btmgmt, btmon, bleak, bettercap.

Options:
  -d, --device INTEGER  Device ID (for multiple CatSniffers)
  --baud INTEGER        Baud rate for serial port  [default: 2000000]
  -v, --verbose         Enable verbose (DEBUG) logging
  -h, --help            Show this message and exit.
